answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or access valuable work. A mirror of the same operator’s accounts does not multiply influence: rewards and voting weight are capped by the total stake, while proven fraud burns the deposit. The attacker must therefore tie up real capital for every identity and risk losing it, making mass fake accounts costly rather than free. A vine of linked accounts still faces the same stake requirement, and a ridge of honest users can challenge suspicious behavior.
